title: Wendy and the Hat for a Sunflower
synopsis: Wendy visits the garden after the radish sprouts open their first leaves and a sunflower shoot appears; the children make pretend hats for the sign rather than placing paper on the plant.
continuity_state: Before: Three tiny radish shoots are visible. Sunflower row still bare. Todd has visited; Wendy has not yet visited the planted garden. Wendy keeps blue ribbon on straw hat. After: A few more days have passed. Radish cotyledons have opened; one sunflower shoot is visible in back. Wendy visits with Aunt Kay; blue ribbon on her hat remains intact. Children draw pretend plant hats on paper, adults keep paper off the seedling; the separate ribbon from the biscuit parcel and paper props return indoors. Garden sign stays bare; oat biscuits shared indoors.

related_resources.reason: University of Minnesota Extension discusses adequate light for seedlings; paper coverings on the emerging shoot are intentionally kept separate from the plant.
The mock mayor title and hat designs are original make-believe play; AAP clinical guidance provides context, not outcome evidence.
